item.title: Survive The Swarm Codes (October 2026)
item.description:
Fighting off waves of enemies is the main challenge in Survive The Swarm , a Roblox RPG where you build your character, collect resources, and try to survive against increasingly dangerous swarms. You can improve your abilities, unlock new options, and strengthen your setup as you progress through the game. Finding a good way to handle each wave is important when the enemies start getting tougher.

The codes below can give you Eggs, Essence, and Gold to help with your progression. You can use these rewards to improve your character, unlock useful upgrades, and get more resources without having to earn everything through regular gameplay. They are a simple way to pick up some extra items before your next run.

Updated October 8, 2026, by Artur Novichenko: A new Survive The Swarm code has just been released, offering an Egg, Essence, and Gold as rewards. This fresh bonus gives you additional resources to support your progression. Be sure to redeem the new code before it expires so you don't miss out on the available rewards. Check back later for more new codes and future updates to the list.

Codes matter in this game because Gold and Essence feed almost everything you want to do. Weapons and gear cost Gold. Evolutions need you to keep playing and keep spending. A raid boss even shows up in the lobby every three hours, and the player who deals the most damage walks away with extra loot. Extra Gold from a code can get you ready for that fight a lot sooner. Essence is handy when you want to push a class or a build instead of waiting through another long run.

Weekly updates keep this Roblox game moving, so new codes often show up around those patches. Redeem what you see today, then hop back in and spend the rewards on something that helps you last longer against the swarm.

How to Redeem Survive The Swarm Codes

  • Open Survive The Swarm on Roblox .
  • Wait until your character loads into the lobby.
  • Look around the screen for a Store button.
  • Tap that button and find the empty code box at the very bottom.
  • Paste one code from the list above.
  • Press the redeem button and wait for the rewards to show up.
  • Repeat with the next code, since each code only works once per account.

If a code grants no rewards, check the spelling first. Codes are picky about capital letters and extra spaces.

How to Get More Survive The Swarm Codes

  • You can find exclusive promo codes shared in the official Discord server.
  • The game page asks you to like the experience and join the creator group FAKT for support and updates.

The easiest habit you can get into for new codes is to check this article every so often. We refresh the list when a new code drops and move old ones to the expired section, so you do not have to hunt through chats just to see what still works.

item.title: Say Hello to Forza Horizon 6's Weirdest Permanent Souvenir Yet
item.description:
The newest Forza Horizon 6 update is called Horizon Meets, and it brings a surprising collaboration to the open-world racing game: 7-Eleven. Forza Horizon 6 may be in a specific niche, but it's been one of the best-reviewed games of the year so far. Now it has been out for several months, Horizon Meets offers one of the biggest updates that the game has seen in its first year.

This collaboration might seem out of place at first, but 7-Eleven stores and car culture actually have a fun history. The convenient store chain has become a global hub for car meet-ups, and Forza Horizon 6 's newest update pays tribute to one of the more unique sides of the car-loving community. These kinds of meet-ups originated in Tokyo, and since Forza Horizon 6 is set in Japan, it only makes sense for Horizon Meets to be centered around a 7-Eleven car gathering.

New Forza-Like Steam Game Launches to Strong, 96% Positive Reviews

A brand-new driving game releases on Steam to exceedingly positive reviews for players looking for a relaxing gameplay experience.

By Diana Velásquez Vargas

Forza Horizon 6's Horizon Meets Event May Be Temporary, But Specific 7-Eleven Content Is Here to Stay

Before players get too excited, I have to make it clear that the meet-up itself is only a limited-time event. Sure, there is plenty of time and space for more meet-ups to be added down the road, but players hoping that the 7-Eleven gathering would be a permanent fixture might be a little disappointed. There is still good news, though. Beyond the in-game convenient store meet-up, the Horizon Meets update introduces even more Forza Horizon 6 fixes, a new round of cars, and 7-Eleven-inspired gear that will remain part of the game, even after the meet-up comes to an end.

Everything to Know About Forza Horizon 6's 7-Eleven Team-Up

  • Festival Playlist unlocks on October 8
  • The 7-Eleven car meet can be found near the Nangan Day Trip.
  • The store overlooks Mount Fuji.
  • A photo challenge during the first week of the Festival Playlist unlocks a 7-Eleven clerk uniform.
  • Three cars can be found for sale behind the 7-Eleven: 2008 Mazda Furai , 1989 Toyota MR2 SC , and 1998 Mercedes-Benz AMG CLK GTR .
  • Festival Playlist cars include a 2018 DeBerti Ford Mustang GT , 2004 Saleen S7 , 2025 BMW M4 CS , 2000 Honda Prelude Type SH , and a 1968 Holden Monaro GTS 327 .
  • 7-Eleven Konbini Prop Pack that can be used for EventLab, Garage and Estate creations.
  • Egg Salad Sandwich Collectible
  • 2 new badges
  • New Treasure Car: 1970 Citroen 2CV
  • Horizon Play adds 200 new levels and 20 new Player Badges

So, even though the 7-Eleven car meet only lasts for a short while, there is at least plenty of new Forza Horizon 6 content to get excited about. The Forza Horizon games are no stranger to wild crossovers. High-profile collaborations with franchises like Halo and the Barbie movie are some of the first few that come to mind, but this 7-Eleven update has the benefit of being both wonderfully weird and actually meaningful, since it's relevant to car culture.

The Horizon Meets Update Adds Some Fun 7-Eleven Goodies to Forza Horizon 6

Once the hype has died down and the car meet-up has come and gone, players will still be able to have fun with a variety of 7-Eleven-inspired rewards. Fans of the Forza Horizon 6 Estate, EventLab, and Garage features get to play around with a special Prop Pack directly inspired by the iconic convenience store.

Everything in Forza Horizon 6's 7-Eleven Prop Pack

  • Signs & Flags : 3 7-Eleven flag variants, plus a small and tall 7-Eleven sign
  • Festival : 3 E-Z UP Tent variants, 7-Eleven tent
  • Urban : 7-Eleven storefront and vending machine, Shop Storage with 3 variants
  • Roads & Racing : 7-Eleven barrier
  • Wall & Fences : Metal Railing 3

After the car meet-up is long gone, players can still use the convenient store props in the three aforementioned game modes, which lessens the blow of it being a limited-time event. Players will need to rev up their best Forza Horizon 6 cars and head to the Nangan region in order to get a taste of the meet-up while it's live; then they can build a fun homage afterward.

Forza Horizon 6's Horizon Meets Is a Needed Breather From Fable Discourse

Playground Games has had its hands full lately. Not only is the developer responsible for one of the most well-received games of 2026, but the studio also has its long-awaited new Fable game on the way. Playground Games' decision to take on a franchise reboot of this scale after solely working on racing games is a bold step forward for the developer. As exciting as Fable is, though, the discourse surrounding the game has kind of overshadowed how good Forza Horizon 6 is, so it's nice to see the racing title back in the spotlight for a moment.

Say Hello to Forza Horizon 6's Weirdest Permanent Souvenir Yet
Forza Horizon 6 Confirms PS5 Release Date, Pre-Orders, and New Expansion
Forza Horizon 6 PS5 Release Date Leaked
Ruriko-Ji Temple FH6 Location

It remains to be seen if Playground Games can move beyond the racing genre once Fable 's release date arrives in February 2027. Regardless of how the open-world fantasy RPG is received, Forza Horizon 6 's new update is a solid example of what Playground Games excels at: making fun-filled open worlds worth exploring.

9 /10

item.title: Steam Officially Makes 3 Games 100% Free Until ~October 12
item.description:
Steam' s Free Weekend selection is giving PC gamers a handful of games to check out this weekend, including a highly-rated open-world survival-crafting co-op game in Core Keeper this weekend. It's worth noting that this Free Weekend promotion is a little more scattered than usual, as typically games expire on the following Monday at 10 am PT/1 pm ET (October 12 this time around) . While that's true for one of the Free Weekend games, specific expiration date/times are listed below because they are a little disparate.

For those new to Steam's Free Weekend promotion, it's pretty simple. Typically on Thursday (although it can vary), Steam makes a handful of paid, premium games 100% free-to-play for a time. There's almost always a steep discount on these games after Steam's Free Weekend too, for anyone who enjoyed a specific game that much.

Xbox Officially Makes 7 Games 100% Free Until October 11, Includes 2025's Best Multiplayer Game

Xbox's Free Play Days officially returns with one of its biggest selections of games in recent months.

By Joshua Duckworth

Steam Free Weekend Games List (October 8-October 12)

Steam's Free Weekend games can vary anywhere from 1-2 games to 5 games+, but this weekend is aiming for that sweet spot in the middle, it seems, with ARC Raiders, Core Keeper , and Squad 44 making up this weekend's free promotion games. Alongside core info like the discount, how long to beat, and links to each free game, the items are listed below to help readers decide which games to play for the promotion.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Round 1

More Games

Steam Free Weekend Game: ARC Raiders

ARC Raiders drops players into a post-apocalyptic world where humanity has been forced underground by a mysterious army of deadly machines. As a Raider, players venture to the surface alone or with a squad to search abandoned areas for weapons, resources, and valuable loot while avoiding or fighting the ARC machines and other players. Every ARC Raiders expedition is a risk, since surviving the journey and successfully extracting with supplies is just as important as finding them in the first place. With customizable gear, dynamic encounters, and a mix of PvE and PvP combat, ARC Raiders turns each trip into a tense fight over how much can be collected before it is time to get out.

  • Release Date : October 30, 2025
  • Genre : Extraction Shooter
  • Developer : Embark Studios
  • Publisher : Embark Studios
  • Steam Review Rating : 81% Very Positive (200K+ User Reviews)
  • Can you beat it before the Promotion ends ? No.
  • Purchase Discount: -50% Off until October 15 ($39.99-->$19.99)
  • Steam Link : Play ARC Raiders for Free until October 12 at 1 am PT/4 am ET

Steam Free Weekend Game: Core Keeper

Core Keeper turns underground caverns into one of Steam's best open-world survival-crafting games, dropping players into a mysterious world where digging deeper is the key to uncovering what happened to the civilization that came before. Mining through the darkness provides the resources needed to craft better equipment, expand a customizable base, grow crops, fish, and prepare for the dangerous creatures and massive bosses lurking throughout the caves. Exploration gradually o pens up new biomes and secrets, while progression gives players more powerful tools to push even farther underground, fulfilling all the major conventions of the genre. Whether played solo or with friends, Core Keeper is built around that constant pull of finding out what is waiting just beyond the next wall (and whether it is something worth fighting).

  • Release Date : August 27, 2024
  • Genre : Open-World Survival Co-Op Game
  • Developer : Pugstorm
  • Publisher : Fireshine Games
  • Steam Review Rating : 94% Very Positive (20K+ User Reviews)
  • Can you beat it before the Promotion ends ? At roughly 30 hours, it's not likely
  • Purchase Discount: -40% Until October 22 ($19.99-->$11.99)
  • Steam Link : Play Core Keeper Free on Steam until October 12 at 10 am PT/1 pm ET

Steam Free Weekend: Squad 44

Squad 44 is a hardcore World War 2 tactical shooter built around large-scale battles where teamwork and communication matter just as much as shooting straight. Players can step into roles ranging from infantry and medics to machine gunners, engineers, and tank crews, with battles unfolding across historically inspired maps filled with trenches, villages, forests, and open fields. Vehicles, artillery, logistics, and defensive positions all become part of the fight, while realistic weapon handling and a slower pace make charging into combat without a plan a quick way to end up dead.

  • Release Date : August 9, 2018
  • Genre : Military Simulation
  • Developer : Offworld
  • Publisher : Offworld
  • Steam Review Rating : 79% Mostly Positive (11K User Reviews)
  • Can you beat it before the Promotion ends ? There's no real "campaign" to beat
  • Purchase Discount: -70% until October 15 ($19.99-->$5.99)
  • Steam Link : Play Squad 44 Free on Steam until October 13 at 10 am PT/1 pm ET

item.title: 8 Open-World RPGs With Endgames Strong Enough to Outlast the Main Story
item.description:
While many games strive to impress players during the initial hours, certain titles aren’t afraid to save their best parts for later. This is often true for combat-focused open-world RPGs, many of which are lengthy enough on their own but still include robust endgame content aimed at high-level characters. Only once you’re familiar with the core mechanics are you finally ready to tackle the hardest, most imaginative challenges in the game.

The approach to endgame varies from game to game, but many titles go to great lengths to rival the main story with their high-level challenges and post-story activities. Some even turn things upside down with their ending, while others are built with almost endless replayability in mind from the get-go. Below are some of the best open-world RPGs that provide enough reasons to stick with them long after completing their main stories, with additional challenges waiting for the most prepared players.

We're counting games with open-zone maps.

Diablo 4

Ever-Evolving Open World Brimming With Activities

Like any decent loot-focused ARPG, Diablo 4 is all about the endgame, with the main story serving as a lengthy introduction to activities players can enjoy for hundreds of hours. With its vast open world and seasonal nature, Diablo 4 is meant to be played for years to come. Even following the Diablo 5 announcement, Blizzard has more content planned for the current title, so there’s little reason to put your favorite builds to rest just yet.

8 RPGs With The Best Endgames

Even after the credits roll, there's still plenty to do in these engaging role-playing games.

3
By Ritwik Mitra

Beyond pushing into higher Torment difficulties with new seasonal builds, Diablo 4 keeps you busy with Lair Bosses, Nightmare Dungeons, Helltides, and The Pit, while systems like Tempering, Masterworking, and Runewords give the equipment chase plenty of depth. The expansions take that loop further: Vessel of Hatred adds the cooperative Dark Citadel and loot-focused Undercity, while Lord of Hatred lets you chain activities together through customizable War Plans. For those who really want to test their limits, Echoing Hatred throws relentless demonic waves at your build until something finally gives.

Elden Ring

A Wealth of Content That Speaks for Itself

Like many open-world RPGs, Elden Ring doesn’t change things drastically after completing the main story path, but the game doesn’t really need to. With its sheer scope, abundance of unique enemies and bosses, entire hidden areas with great loot rewards, and endlessly cryptic storytelling, it’s hard to imagine players seeing everything it has to offer by simply reaching one of its several endings.

6 Best Open-World Games With Plenty To Do After The Story Ends

These open-world titles offer robust endgame content and plenty of side activities to keep players engaged long after the main story.

By Vlad Mazanko

Only a small fraction of Elden Ring’s bosses are necessary to reach the ending, leaving an enormous amount of optional content to track down afterward. Some of its toughest foes are buried deep in hidden areas, giving you plenty of reasons to keep strengthening your character and upgrading your gear. A thorough first playthrough can stretch toward 200 hours, even before the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, which can easily rival a full-fledged RPG in scope and length.

Assassin’s Creed Shadows

Among the Most Suitable for Endless Play in the Series

Assassin’s Creed Shadows is hardly the first game that comes to mind when thinking of near-endlessly replayable open-world RPGs, yet it packs several aces up its sleeve, especially thanks to Ubisoft’s final title updates. AC Shadows’ world is truly enormous, with dozens of targets to track down and assassinate, many stretching well beyond the main story that follows the Shinbakufu. Some players might even miss the entirely optional Templar hunt questline that unlocks very late in the game.

After Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, Ubisoft's Next Remake Feels Obvious

Black Flag Resynced proves Ubisoft can modernize a classic without losing what made it special, but another AC game needs that treatment far more.

By Josh Cotts

Still, the main attraction for continued play is how its in-game seasons keep giving you reasons to return, with Corrupted Castles and refreshing contracts offering new challenges and rewards. The final AC Shadows update also added Domains: replayable challenges across five distinct maps with changing modifiers, altered bosses, and exclusive equipment rewards. Their higher difficulties can encourage you to rethink your entire combat build, even before trying Nightmare difficulty or NG+.

Dragon’s Dogma 2

Unique Twist on the Endgame With a Changing World

Dragon’s Dogma 2’s main appeal is its strong emergent gameplay, which, coupled with an exquisite combat system featuring multiple vocations and the unique Pawn system, yields truly captivating results. Another notable trait of this combat-driven open-world RPG is its special approach to endgame. Pursuing the true ending takes you beyond the showdown with the Dragon and into the more challenging Unmoored World, with intriguing lore revelations and a familiar map transformed.

Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen's Endgame Has Shadow of the Erdtree's Best Trick

Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is borrowing one of Shadow of the Erdtree's smartest endgame ideas to keep veteran players exploring.

By Nikol Nikolova

Here, tougher enemies are only part of the picture. A crimson apocalyptic haze changes the entire look and feel of DD2’s world, while dried seabeds reveal previously unreachable areas. New bosses and urgent evacuation quests give exploration a different purpose, turning this final stretch into much more than another round of monster hunting. This shift also reflects a meta-narrative twist on the cyclical nature of the Arisen and Dragon standoff, giving you enough reasons to experience the world anew. And the brand-new Dark Arisen expansion only strengthens the appeal, adding more adventures and challenges to keep playing for.

Final Fantasy 15

Saving Some of Its Best Parts for After the Story

Another open-world RPG that probably won’t come to mind immediately, Final Fantasy 15 treats endgame in its own way, saving some of the best content for later. Given how enormous FF15 is on its own, it’s hard to tell how many players will even finish it to reach that point, but that’s an entirely different question. The game’s post-game includes several substantial additions: the sealed Menace Beneath Lucis dungeons, legendary-weapon quests, and even Pitioss, an unusual dungeon built around puzzles and platforming that challenge you in completely different ways.

7 Action RPGs With Better New Game Plus Modes Than Elden Ring, Ranked

From altered combat scenarios to secret quests, gear, and bosses, these titles give you plenty of reasons to try New Game+ cycles.

2
By Vlad Mazanko

As a result, finishing the story in Final Fantasy 15 opens access to substantial challenges you couldn’t complete earlier. A great example is obtaining the flying Regalia Type-F: it’s only possible after the main story, once you bring the required parts from the Imperial base to Cindy. Very few games would even dare to lock such an exciting feature behind the ending, but it seems things only start to get serious in FF15 after beating the final boss.

Monster Hunter: World

Designed for Almost Endless Replayability

Few series are built with endless replayability in mind quite like Monster Hunter . With its deeply interlocking hunting and crafting mechanics, a wealth of locations, and unique monsters to defeat, Monster Hunter: World is surely one of those games designed for continuous play rather than beating its main story and moving on to something else.

In fact, Monster Hunter: World’s main narrative serves more as a lengthy prologue to the mechanical depth that follows once you begin to fully grasp its elaborate combat system. Luckily, there are enough challenges to tackle even for seasoned hunters with high-end gear, with Iceborne doubling down on the original’s captivating endgame. Its Guiding Lands tie ongoing hunts to valuable materials for further equipment upgrades, while the toughest late-game monsters give all that preparation a proper purpose.

For even more open areas, you are always welcome in Monster Hunter Wilds , which shares much of the same hunt-and-craft appeal.

Middle-earth: Shadow of War

Fully Capitalizing on Its Unique Gameplay Strengths

By any standard, Middle-earth: Shadow of War is a huge open-world game with plenty of things to do. Its biggest allure is the gameplay loop itself, bolstered by ongoing Nemesis rivalries, and the story’s epilogue makes full use of that. Capturing territory during the campaign is one thing, but once Shadow Wars shifts the focus toward defending your fortresses and maintaining your army, the experience takes on a different rhythm. The updated version streamlines this stretch considerably, letting you reach the true ending without the original’s lengthy siege grind.

6 RPGs Where A Hero Becomes The Final Villain

A hero becoming the villain is a pretty common trope in games, but some RPGs still pull it off exceptionally well, often in ways all their own.

3
By Vlad Mazanko

For fans who still can’t get enough of Shadow of War’s satisfying combat and army management, Endless Siege keeps the fortress battles going after the credits. You can recruit better captains, claim stronger gear, and keep refining your defenses or taking on other players’ fortresses through Online Conquests. All the while, the Nemesis system continues producing betrayals, unexpected returns, and rivalries so personal you won’t experience them elsewhere.

Tom Clancy’s The Division 2

Alive and Kicking Even Seven Years Later

Just like Diablo 4 , The Division 2 shows no signs of stopping, enjoying robust support from Massive for over seven years now. Still one of the best open-world looter-shooter-slash-RPGs on the market, it’s so generous with content, activities, and game modes that most fans probably forget how long it’s been since they last played through its original story missions.

The Division 2’s campaign establishes your character and the ever-changing world before the Black Tusk invasion sends you back to reclaim Washington. Pretty soon, refining builds and tackling increasingly demanding activities become the real attraction. Legendary missions, raids, Incursions, Countdown, and The Summit give that equipment chase meaningful destinations, while territory battles, projects, events, and bounties keep the wheel turning. Some of the toughest content requires a team, but there’s still plenty to sustain solo players too, especially with another story DLC, Echoes of Central Park , launching this November. Agents, assemble!

item.title: 10 Years Later, Stardew Valley Is Finally Outgrowing Its Own Ending
item.description:
Video games exist in so many different forms and genres, but one thing that ties a lot of them together is the concept of an ending or a logical stopping point. While games like Stardew Valley might not have a traditional climax, aside from a nice credit roll for achieving perfection, many people find themselves putting the game down once they reach a certain level of satisfaction. You might decide that after marriage, kids, and burning through the dozens of checklists, it is time to hang it up, but ConcernedApe is deciding to question those existing endpoints and potentially open the doors for far more content down the line.

What we know so far comes from a teaser riddle that states "two paths will be extended, three will become four, the mermaid's fruit will go free", alongside a few other improvements to the family system. As obscure as that may be, there has been a steady stream of family-related information teases that have led many to believe that Stardew Valley may be getting far more than just a couple of content additions. Instead, there could be a world where your existing save files with dozens of hours could suddenly have a lot more to do, as those previous paths that were once stopping points now become extended into something more.

ConcernedApe Makes Public Announcement for Stardew Valley's 1.7 Update

Developer ConcernedApe publicly announces a few cryptic details for Stardew Valley's 1.7 update.

By Joshua Duckworth

Stardew Valley 1.7 Changes How We See the End

Cozy farming games often follow a very similar formula to one another when it comes to deciding when the game ends. It doesn't matter if the goal is to expand your land into the horizon or to complete hundreds of individual quests; at some point, you are going to feel happy with your creation and the work you have done with the people, and either choose to start all over again or to move on to something else. For Stardew Valley , the game has had quite a few incremental updates that have added content at all tiers of play, some affecting your entire journey and others focusing more on late-game additions and systems that pad out those longer save files with a little more game time.

However, even as you farm all these new crops and attend the different festivals and events, the inevitability of the end is always looming. After marrying a villager and having children, the game effectively slows to a halt, as the kids remain at a certain age and everything else like farming becomes a cyclical act of upkeep instead of having any sense of progress. That's why so many people start over or introduce mods into the game, choosing to leave their existing world in this end state and create a new one where they can try different approaches or experiment in ways they never thought to before.

There could be a world where your existing save files with dozens of hours could suddenly have a lot more to do, as those previous paths that were once stopping points now become extended into something more.

That's exactly what makes this new 1.7 update so interesting, as the wording is very specifically referencing this issue of late-game conclusions. People have frequently taken issue with the way relationships are handled in Stardew Valley , as while it is nice to be able to marry and to follow that arc far beyond friendship, it still ends up hitting a wall down the line once you have effectively finished building out your life. So, if certain paths are being extended, then that could mean this decade-old goal may be replaced by another end state, with its own set of milestones for people to strive for across all their save files.

Additionally, by extending the playtime beyond the softer endings that appear in the late game, it encourages a lot of people to return who have otherwise left to play newer, more expansive games. Your kids may end up becoming a much larger part of the story and experience, or the new marriage options may introduce countless routes to take that can only be accessed in those relationships, but most importantly, it gives longtime players a more engaging kind of content that isn't just another fish to catch or another crop to harvest.

Haunted Chocolatier Is the Question Hanging Over Stardew Valley's Future

As great as it is to hear about all these new Stardew Valley updates, there is still a sweet-flavored elephant in the room that remains a topic of debate. ConcernedApe's upcoming game, Haunted Chocolatier, has been talked about sparingly, but what we do know is that the gameplay style is very akin to the developer's original project, which begs the question as to when development for one game ends to focus on the other.

As of right now, attention is clearly being placed onto this newer project. ConcernedApe is putting everything into Haunted Chocolatier, and Stardew Valley is taking a backseat, at least in terms of his involvement. There are already a few additional team members helping with updates for Stardew Valley, and as time goes on, it is hard to tell just how the content will be split between the two games. I can see a world where, whenever this new game drops, it sees a similar pace of content updates over the coming years, but, with only so many hands on deck, it may come at a cost.

Given how successful Stardew Valley has been up until this point, after the next few updates, the devs may decide that it is time to move on and place their development efforts on something new for people to get excited about. This problem is far from new, and we even saw it most recently with Diablo 4 , where the sequel comes in and almost instantly axes any chances of future content for the existing game. However, Stardew Valley was never set up as a live-service game that was destined to be patched until the end of time, which means that any updates we get from now can be considered bonuses.

10 Years Later, Stardew Valley Is Finally Outgrowing Its Own Ending
"Stardew Valley With a Serial Killer Game" Grave Seasons Finally Announces Release Date
PS5 Officially Getting 9/10 Stardew Valley-Like Life Sim in October
New Open-World Stardew Valley-Like Life Sim Officially Coming to PS5

I think that is what all this boils down to at the end of the day. Stardew Valley is a monumental success, and these continuous updates are a blessing that could go on for another decade or stop with the next release. But regardless of what the future holds, we know that ConcernedApe and all the other people working on the game are simply trying to create the best possible experience for their players, and if they see room for something more, then they are clearly more than happy to jump back in and make the changes. And, as paths are extended and existing ones branch out, who knows, we may eventually see a bridge that takes us from Stardew Valley all the way to Haunted Chocolatier , perhaps not physically but as a way to guide us over to the next chapter.

That's exactly what makes this new 1.7 update so interesting, as the wording is very specifically referencing this issue of late-game conclusions. People have frequently taken issue with the way relationships are handled in Stardew Valley , as while it is nice to be able to marry and to follow that arc far beyond friendship, it still ends up hitting a wall down the line once you have effectively finished building out your life. So, if certain paths are being extended, then that could mean this decade-old goal may be replaced by another end state, with its own set of milestones for people to strive for across all their save files.

Additionally, by extending the playtime beyond the softer endings that appear in the late game, it encourages a lot of people to return who have otherwise left to play newer, more expansive games. Your kids may end up becoming a much larger part of the story and experience, or the new marriage options may introduce countless routes to take that can only be accessed in those relationships, but most importantly, it gives longtime players a more engaging kind of content that isn't just another fish to catch or another crop to harvest.

Haunted Chocolatier Is the Question Hanging Over Stardew Valley's Future

As great as it is to hear about all these new Stardew Valley updates, there is still a sweet-flavored elephant in the room that remains a topic of debate. ConcernedApe's upcoming game, Haunted Chocolatier, has been talked about sparingly, but what we do know is that the gameplay style is very akin to the developer's original project, which begs the question as to when development for one game ends to focus on the other.

As of right now, attention is clearly being placed onto this newer project. ConcernedApe is putting everything into Haunted Chocolatier, and Stardew Valley is taking a backseat, at least in terms of his involvement. There are already a few additional team members helping with updates for Stardew Valley, and as time goes on, it is hard to tell just how the content will be split between the two games. I can see a world where, whenever this new game drops, it sees a similar pace of content updates over the coming years, but, with only so many hands on deck, it may come at a cost.

Given how successful Stardew Valley has been up until this point, after the next few updates, the devs may decide that it is time to move on and place their development efforts on something new for people to get excited about. This problem is far from new, and we even saw it most recently with Diablo 4 , where the sequel comes in and almost instantly axes any chances of future content for the existing game. However, Stardew Valley was never set up as a live-service game that was destined to be patched until the end of time, which means that any updates we get from now can be considered bonuses.

Stardew Valley is a monumental success, and these continuous updates are a blessing that could go on for another decade or stop with the next release. But regardless of what the future holds, we know that ConcernedApe and all the other people working on the game are simply trying to create the best possible experience for their players, and if they see room for something more, then they are clearly more than happy to jump back in and make the changes. And, as paths are extended and existing ones branch out, who knows, we may eventually see a bridge that takes us from Stardew Valley all the way to Haunted Chocolatier , perhaps not physically but as a way to guide us over to the next chapter.
